name: The Bail Project
summary: A US nonprofit, set up in 2016 in Venice, California, and bailing people out since 2018, that pays bail through a national revolving fund for people who can't afford it, supports them until their cases close (court reminders, rides, referrals), runs community-release pilots where cash bail has ended, and campaigns against laws that expand pretrial detention or restrict charitable bail. In the year to June 2024 it spent $14.5 million, at 17 bail sites in 12 states (14 sites a year later).

spending.source: https://bailproject.org/annualreport2024 (Annual Report 2024, Financials, pp. 50-51: total program expenses $10,460,596 of total expenses $14,464,653, fiscal year July 2023 to June 2024; the audited Form 990 for the same year reports one programme of $10,359,791 and total expenses of $14,332,906, IRS e-file 202510589349301416). Fiscal 2024 is the latest year with a programme split and reach: the 2025 report and Form 990 (year to June 2025, total expenses $16,254,891 in the audited statements) give neither.
